scenes.text: Five hundred years ago… in the desert town of Merta, in Rajasthan… a little girl named Meera was born into a royal family.
The story goes that a wandering sadhu once placed a small idol of Krishna in her hands. And from that day… she never let it go.
She talked to him. She sang to him. She fell asleep holding him. Krishna… Giridhar Gopal, the lifter of the mountain… was hers.
Other children played with dolls. Meera played with her Gopal… and grew up believing he was her truest friend in the whole world.
When she grew up, Meera was married into the royal house of Mewar… and brought to the great fort of Chittor.
She became a princess of one of the proudest families in India. But under her veil… she still carried her little Krishna, everywhere.
Every night she went to the temple. She sang. She danced. She sat with wandering saints… as if no one else in the world was watching.
But in a royal court, someone is always watching. The courtiers began to whisper. A queen… singing in public? Dancing with beggars and saints?
Her own family felt ashamed of her. They told her to stop. To worship the family's goddess. To behave… like a queen.
Meera listened to all of them. And then, gently, she said no. My heart already belongs to someone, she said. I cannot give it twice.
Then her husband was killed in battle. Meera was young… and now she was alone, in a palace that did not want her.
In those days, a widow was expected to follow her husband into the funeral fire. The story goes that Meera refused. My Lord is alive, she said… I am not a widow.
Log kahe Meera bhai baawri. People say Meera has gone mad. She wrote those words herself… in one of her songs.
The story goes that one day, a cup was sent to her. They called it holy water. Everyone in the palace knew… it was poison.
Meera offered it to Krishna first… as she offered everything. Then she drank it. And she lived.
Another time, they sent her a basket of flowers… with a snake hidden inside. When she lifted the lid, the story goes, she found only a garland.
Meera heard every word they said about her. It hurt. She was not made of stone. But she never… stopped… singing.
Pag ghungroo baandh Meera naachi re. Meera tied the bells on her ankles…
and she danced. In the courtyard, in front of everyone who had laughed at her. Not to prove them wrong. Just because her heart was full.
In the end, she left the palace behind. She walked to Vrindavan, Krishna's own land… singing all the way.
Mere to Giridhar Gopal, doosro na koi. My only one is Giridhar Gopal… there is no other.
The story goes that she reached Dwarka, by the sea… and sang one last song in Krishna's temple. And she was never seen again.
Five hundred years later, her songs are still sung… in homes, in temples, in schools, all over India.
And the people who whispered about her? No one remembers their names.
Krishna says in the Gita… The one who stays the same in blame and in praise… quiet, content, steady of mind… that one is dear to me.
